name: HTML, CSS & JavaScript
subtitle: The web's three core languages (no framework)
creator: Tim Berners-Lee (HTML, 1991), Håkon Wium Lie (CSS, 1994), Brendan Eich (JavaScript, 1995)
description: Every website, whatever framework it uses, ends up as HTML (structure), CSS (appearance) and JavaScript (behavior) in the browser. Writing them directly, without a framework, is the best way to understand what frameworks do for you, and it's all you need for simple sites.

concepts.explanation: Rules that pick elements and style them.
The live tree of elements that JavaScript can change.
click, input and submit trigger your code.
Ask a server for data without reloading.
Layouts that adapt to phone and desktop.

codeSamples.label: HTML + JavaScript
codeSamples.code:
<button id="like">Like (0)</button>

<script>
  let likes = 0;
  const button = document.getElementById("like");
  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    likes++;
    button.textContent = `Like (${likes})`;
  });
</script>

cons: Large apps get hard to organize
You hand-write updates to the page
No component system out of the box
